clue.text: London's growth in profit

parts.note: London is the capital city of the UK, so it stands for the word capital
a growth or increase is a gain

explanation.surface: A remark about how much London's earnings have risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word; the surface reads 'growth in profit' as one phrase, but the definition is just 'profit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital gain is money made when an asset is sold for more than it cost, a kind of profit.

clue.text: Teachers show pain

indicators.note: the word Teachers is made to show, or display, a shorter word sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Teachers demonstrate that they are suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a verb of display in the surface; here it says the answer is visible within 'Teachers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, lasting pain.

clue.text: A nagging wish to decapitate an evil woman

indicators.note: cutting off the head means removing the first letter of the word for an evil woman

parts.note: a spiteful woman is insultingly called a bitch

explanation.surface: Someone longs to behead a wicked woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a persistent restless craving or desire.

clue.text: Thanks for getting up exhausted and dressed!

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word for thanks is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you
exhausted means tired

explanation.surface: A tired person thanks someone for getting them out of bed and clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' sounds like rising from bed; in this down entry it reverses TA to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired means clothed or wearing particular garments.

clue.text: Increase beam when moving left to right

indicators.note: the letter standing for left is swapped out and the letter for right takes its place

parts.note: to beam is to glow, shining with light or happiness

explanation.surface: Advice about sliding a beam sideways to make it bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) in GLOW becomes R (right). The surface suggests physical movement across a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to become larger, to rise in size or amount.

clue.text: The little devil takes action — and crashes

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
to take action is to act, so he acts

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite goes into action and causes collisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacts are collisions, forceful strikes of one thing against another.

clue.text: Silly old nun with valid lawsuit? Not at all

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish elderly nun brings a lawsuit she thinks is sound, but it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two stretches of fodder; the closing words say the lawsuit is not valid at all, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action described as having no force at all is without legal effect, invalid.

clue.text: Arrange for transport to run

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is an old form of transport
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Organising for a bus to operate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage-manage something is to organise or orchestrate it behind the scenes.

clue.text: Diamonds found in court case

definitions.meaning: diamonds is one of the four ... in a pack of cards
a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.surface: Jewels turn up during a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a set of playing cards marked with one symbol, and legal proceedings brought against someone.

clue.text: Hairdressers on the attack?

parts.note: people who deal with shocks of hair imagined as an attacking force of soldiers

explanation.surface: Barbers going on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock is a thick mass of hair, so hairdressers become troops who handle shocks; the real sense is soldiers trained to lead assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Shock troops are elite soldiers used for sudden assaults, here reimagined as stylists of thick hair.

clue.text: Get weary of the paving stone

definitions.meaning: a ..., or flagstone, is a flat slab used for paving

explanation.surface: Becoming tired of a slab underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to lose strength and tire, and a flat slab laid as a pavement.

clue.text: She puts back "out in order" to evade responsibility

indicators.note: letters that are put out and then in order are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman returns something marked out of service to dodge blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass the buck is to shift blame or a duty onto someone else.

clue.text: Deliver hire car late and settle the difference

indicators.note: deliver is read as freeing the letters so they emerge in a different sequence

explanation.surface: Returning a rental car overdue and paying what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle the difference' suggests paying an extra charge; here it means resolving a disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear the air is to resolve a dispute or tension by talking it through.

clue.text: Finished with a B-boyfriend?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Finished with a B-boyfriend? (3,4)': A + L (learner) + LOVER would need 'L-boyfriend'; no parse gives the B, and searching the exact text found nothing.

clue.text: Lightning attack — quietly slipped in

indicators.note: the letter for quietly is slipped in, inserted into the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A sudden assault in which something was sneaked in quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightning used as an adjective means very fast, swift.

clue.text: Starts to use massage on back bone

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words means their first letters are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin massaging someone's spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back bone' reads as the spine, but 'back' is STERN and 'bone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Flogs magic formulas to release cash

indicators.note: releasing the coin means letting it go out of the word for magic formulas

parts.note: spells are magic formulas
P, a penny, is a small piece of British cash

explanation.surface: Someone sells magic charms to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogs' looks like beating; it is British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog something, in British slang, is to sell it.

clue.text: Valleys provided shelter for suicidal escapee

indicators.note: the words suicidal escapee shelter, or house, a shorter word inside them

explanation.surface: Remote valleys hid a desperate runaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'suicidal' and 'escapee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dales are valleys, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Break off for a photograph

explanation.surface: Pausing work to take a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to break suddenly with a crack, and a quick informal picture.

clue.text: Banker gets star backing

indicators.note: backing means the word for star is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A financier wins the support of a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword slang for a river, something with banks; the Avon is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so in crosswords a banker can mean a river such as the Avon.

clue.text: Accommodation for five sick top astronauts

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ill means sick

indicators.note: the top of astronauts is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lodgings for five unwell leading spacefarers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top astronauts' suggests the best ones; 'top' takes only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a house, often a holiday home, providing a place to stay.

clue.text: Drifter who's against a subsidy

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
a grant is a subsidy

explanation.surface: A tramp who opposes state handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a homeless wanderer, someone who drifts from place to place.

clue.text: Tipsy school-leaver veers off for more drink, possibly

indicators.note: tipsy suggests the letters stagger about and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk graduate swerves off in search of another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of 'veers' away ('off') from 'school-leaver'; the remaining CHOOLLA are rearranged. 'for more' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is the intoxicating substance in beer, wine and spirits, an example of something one might drink.

clue.text: He had to change, being the impetuous type

indicators.note: change tells us these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man was forced to adapt, given his rash nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is a rash, quick-tempered person.

clue.text: Place in grass, dispatching…

indicators.note: the word for place goes in, inside, the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing, which is also to sing
to lay is to place or put down

explanation.surface: Putting something in the grass, then sending it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the lawn; it is slang for informing on someone, as is 'sing'. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatching someone means killing them, which is what slaying is.

clue.text: …cattle and grouse

definitions.meaning: ... cattle are bred for meat, and ... can mean such animals
to complain, a grouse being a complaint

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: killing livestock and game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird beside 'cattle'; here it means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: meat from cows, or the animals themselves, and a grumble.

clue.text: Half of them under way? Stop!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: half of the word them is its last two letters

explanation.surface: An order to halt half the people already on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it.

clue.text: Role of section

explanation.surface: An actor's role within a portion of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a character played in a drama, and a portion of a whole.

clue.text: Ban doctor who at last

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word who

explanation.surface: Prohibiting a medic, finally doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor who' tempts as the TV show Doctor Who; the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a prohibition, an official rejection.

clue.text: One might heal her, if at doctor

definitions.text: One might heal her, if at doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are tampered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at the surgery might cure a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone claiming to cure illness by prayer or belief might cure a sick woman.

clue.text: Cut the speed

definitions.meaning: a ... is a rate of movement, as in going at a fast ...

explanation.surface: Reduce the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to trim with scissors, and a brisk pace of motion.

clue.text: Time spent in pretence is a spur to action

indicators.note: the letter for time is spent in, placed inside, the word for pretence

parts.note: a simulation is a pretence or imitation

explanation.surface: Hours wasted on make-believe are what drive us to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulation is encouragement that rouses someone into activity.
